title: Milestone 2026.04.45 Operational Retrospective

slowest_experiments.title: JEPA fast-path gate integration
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Ninth consecutive milestone in the slowest-5. Checkpoint-failure loop — tests failing at commit time triggers full re-read and retry. Exclusion manifest was built this milestone (Exp 589) but conductor_consulted=False (RETRO-067 partial) — Exp 308 re-entered the queue before the manifest was consulted. Until the conductor wire-in is verified, this experiment will continue to re-enter and consume 105 min per cycle.

slowest_experiments.title: Conductor timeout watchdog — RETRO-003 (17+ milestone carry)
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Ninth consecutive milestone in the slowest-5. Exclusion manifest was not consulted when this run was queued (RETRO-067 partial). Although Exp 425 is 'completed', it re-enters because the conductor has no mechanism to recognise experiments already resolved in prior cycles.

slowest_experiments.title: CPU-bound benchmark proving GPU need
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Ninth consecutive milestone in the slowest-5. Legacy pre-400 script — no ExperimentTemplate, no BatchedInferenceRunner. Sequential CPU inference loop. Same root cause as .44 close: exclusion manifest was built but conductor_consulted not confirmed before this experiment queued.

slowest_experiments.title: Tier 3 end-to-end self-learning
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Ninth consecutive milestone in the slowest-5. Identical checkpoint-failure state to Exp 308. Both Exps 308 and 309 have been frozen in a failing-test checkpoint since .37. Exclusion manifest must gate both before .46 starts. Combined cost of Exps 308+309 in .45: 171 min — equivalent to 17 median-length experiments.

slowest_experiments.title: Live precision pipeline — 200 GSM8K, 5 variants, 2 models
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Sixth consecutive milestone in the slowest-5. 1,000 sequential inference calls with no BatchedInferenceRunner. BatchedInferenceRunner migration sprints in .41 and .42 produced batching_added=[] for this target both times. A dedicated single-experiment BatchedInferenceRunner migration for Exp 410 (estimated 2 hours) would reduce runtime from 64 min to ~16 min and remove it from the slowest-5 permanently.

bottlenecks_identified: EXCLUSION MANIFEST WIRE-IN INCOMPLETE (RETRO-067): Exp 589 successfully built the exclusion manifest and gated Exps 308, 260, 309, 425, and 410 — the single highest-priority infrastructure action from nine consecutive retros. However, conductor_consulted=False in the Exp 589 result, meaning the manifest was built but the conductor did not consult it before queuing experiments. All five legacy experiments re-entered the queue and consumed the full 385-minute quota again. The build is done; the integration is the remaining blocker. One function call in scripts/research_conductor.py is the delta.

SAME FIVE SLOWEST EXPERIMENTS — NINTH CONSECUTIVE MILESTONE: Exps 308, 260, 309, 425, and 410 appear in the slowest-5 for the ninth consecutive milestone (.37 through .45). Cumulative wasted time since .37 is now approximately 3,255 minutes (54.3 hours). At 385 min/milestone and 9 milestones, this single defect has consumed more total researcher time than the fastest 338 experiments in the project. The exclusion manifest build in .45 (Exp 589) is the first structural intervention; the integration must be verified as complete before any .46 experiment is queued.

DUALGPU UTILIZATION AT ZERO (FOURTH CONSECUTIVE MILESTONE): Both RTX 3090s at 4MB VRAM and 0% utilization at close. GPU 1 contributed 0% of inference compute across every .45 experiment. DualGPU parallel forward-pass (Qwen on GPU 0, Gemma on GPU 1 simultaneously) has been recommended since .36 and demonstrated in zero experiments across four clean-close milestones. The GPU monitor's top suggestion every session is identical: 'Use DualGPURunner.' A single controlled experiment (2-3 hours) would confirm the 1.8-2x throughput gain and validate the recommendation empirically.

BATCHEDINFERENCERUNNER STILL NOT APPLIED TO EXP 410: Three consecutive migration sprints (.41 Exp 547, .42 Exp 547b, .43 Exp 547 scope check) all produced batching_added=[] for Exp 410. The migration framework exists; applying it to one specific experiment has been deferred repeatedly. Exp 410's 1,000 sequential inference calls run at ~3.84 calls/min; at batch_size=8 the same work would complete in ~125 batches at an estimated 3-4x speedup (16-21 min instead of 64 min). The implementation investment is approximately 2 hours against a return of 43-48 min saved per milestone.

COACE OFFLINE/LIVE DISTRIBUTION GAP WORSENED (RETRO-066, RETRO-068): CoACE v3 recall on live data regressed to 4% — lower than v2's 5.9%. The entire verify-repair chain (RETRO-033, RETRO-038, FR-11) remains blocked because the extractor cannot reliably identify arithmetic violations in real model outputs. CoACEV3's architecture was redesigned without first collecting a training corpus of live (model_A_response, model_B_response) pairs. The root cause is training distribution mismatch, not architecture. Exp 578 collected 100 live pairs; they have not been used to retrain the extractor.

PRE-FLIGHT TEST SUITE BLOCKING OVERHEAD: The full cargo test + pytest suite runs as a blocking gate before each experiment commit. At 481 experiments/milestone, if each pre-commit run averages 60 seconds, that is approximately 481 minutes (8.0 hours) of test execution per milestone — roughly 10.5% of total wall time. No incremental test selection is implemented. For experiments that modify a single Python module, running the full suite is a 12x over-investment. This bottleneck grows linearly with the test suite size as the project adds REQ-*/SCENARIO-* coverage.

DOC RECONCILIATION SEQUENTIAL OVERHEAD: Each experiment triggers updates to conductor-log.md, changelog.md, ops/status.md, and traceability.md in sequence. At 481 experiments, fully sequential doc-reconciliation adds approximately 481 * (avg write time) to milestone wall time. The .44 retro estimated 30-45 minutes of savings from batching doc updates to end-of-phase. This was not implemented in .45. The same estimate holds: batching every 3-5 experiments eliminates 60-80% of per-experiment doc-update tool calls.

CONTEXT DEBT MULTIPLIER ON LONG-CARRY RETROS: RETRO-033 has now carried 13+ attempts without closure. RETRO-038 has carried 9+ attempts. Each new attempt requires re-reading prior attempt result files to reconstruct context, adding 10-20 min of overhead before any implementation work begins. The two-milestone carry-limit rule (recommended in .40, .41, .42, .43, .44 retros) has still not been enforced as a conductor rule.
improvements_suggested: VERIFY EXCLUSION MANIFEST CONDUCTOR WIRE-IN BEFORE ANY .46 EXPERIMENT (RETRO-067 — Phase 0, mandatory): Exp 589 built scripts/conductor_exclusion_manifest.json successfully. The remaining delta is verifying that the conductor reads and consults the manifest before queuing any experiment. Check that conductor_consulted=True in the next run against Exps 308, 260, 309, 425, and 410. This single verification step converts a 54-hour accumulated debt into a permanent 385-min/milestone saving. Estimated implementation time: 30 minutes for the wire-in check. This is the highest-ROI action in the project.

DEDICATED BATCHEDINFERENCERUNNER MIGRATION FOR EXP 410 ONLY: Do not schedule another broad migration sprint. Assign a single-experiment task: open scripts/experiment_410_live_precision.py, identify the inference loop, wrap it with BatchedInferenceRunner(batch_size=8). Verify the result file shows batching_applied=True and duration < 25 min. Estimated implementation: 2 hours. Estimated saving: 43-48 min per milestone (removes Exp 410 from slowest-5 for the first time in 6 milestones).

DEMONSTRATE DUALGPU PARALLEL FORWARD-PASS IN ONE CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT: Schedule 'Exp N: DualGPURunner Smoke Test' as the first GPU experiment in .46. Load Qwen on cuda:0 and Gemma on cuda:1, run 10 forward passes in parallel, measure utilization on both GPUs simultaneously. Accept nothing less than both GPUs above 0% utilization at the same timestamp. This has been deferred for 4 milestones. The smoke test is 1-2 hours; the validation data it produces grounds all future parallelism estimates.

RETRAIN COACE V4 ON LIVE CORPUS (RETRO-066, RETRO-068 — HIGHEST RESEARCH PRIORITY): Exp 578 collected 100 live (question, model_A_response, model_B_response) pairs. Use these pairs as the training corpus for CoACEV4. Do not redesign the architecture until the training distribution is fixed. Target: live recall >= 20% before scheduling any verify-repair experiment. This single action unblocks RETRO-033, RETRO-038, RETRO-064, RETRO-066, RETRO-068, RETRO-069, and FR-11 simultaneously — the entire verify-repair chain.

IMPLEMENT INCREMENTAL TEST SELECTION FOR SINGLE-MODULE EXPERIMENTS: Replace 'pytest tests/python' with 'pytest tests/python -k <module_name>' for experiments that modify a single Python module. Add a conductor hook: when an experiment's changed_files list contains only files under a single python/carnot/ subdirectory, run only tests in the matching tests/python/test_<subdirectory>*.py files. Estimated savings: 255-385 minutes per milestone (first time below 10% test overhead).

BATCH DOC UPDATES TO END-OF-PHASE (NOT END-OF-EXPERIMENT): Change the conductor workflow so that conductor-log.md, changelog.md, and ops/status.md are updated once per phase (every 3-5 experiments) rather than after every experiment. Phase boundaries are already defined in research-roadmap-next.yaml. This eliminates 60-80% of per-experiment doc-write tool calls without losing any fidelity. Estimated saving: 30-45 minutes per milestone.

ENFORCE TWO-MILESTONE RETRO CARRY LIMIT AS CONDUCTOR RULE: Any RETRO item that appears in the slowest-5 for 2 consecutive milestones without closure is automatically added to the exclusion manifest by the conductor. This prevents the 9-milestone drift observed for Exps 308/260/309/425/410. Implement as a Python function in scripts/research_conductor.py that checks the previous retro JSON's slowest_experiments list against the current one and writes any repeats to the manifest before the session starts.

SESSION CONSOLIDATION FOR MICRO-EXPERIMENTS: Experiments that complete in under 5 minutes (spec-update experiments, verification re-runs like Exp 447/18 and 447/19, doc-only turns like Exp 435) should be batched into a single conductor turn. Multiple same-experiment re-verification turns (observed 3x for Exp 447 across sessions in .44/.45 planning context) consume full context-load overhead for zero incremental work. Add a conductor rule: if the prior turn's result file for experiment N has status='success', do not re-enter experiment N in the same milestone.

time_savings_breakdown.note: 13% optimistic upper bound. Historical over-estimation pattern across 8 milestones (.37-.44): projections of 15-25% consistently achieved 0-4%. If conductor_consulted is confirmed True in .46 Phase 0, the 8.3% exclusion manifest saving is the most reliable single prediction in the project.
